name: AI Deep Dive — IONQ — 2026-05-04
rationale: IonQ at $48.02 trades at ~135x TTM revenue of $130M and $17.6B market cap — extreme venture-style pricing for a quantum computing company. Revenue grew 428% YoY, demonstrating genuine commercial traction via AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, and Google Cloud integrations. However, gross margins are declining (73%→40% over 4 years) as hardware costs scale, and net losses deepened to -$510M TTM vs -$331M prior year. The 5-year DCF model (FV $8.54) captures only near-term commercial viability probability — it explicitly undervalues the 10-20 year platform optionality that the market is pricing. IonQ has the strongest commercial position in quantum computing today (real revenue, cloud partnerships, trapped-ion accuracy advantage), but the 5-year model cannot justify the current price. The investment case is a long-horizon speculative bet on trapped-ion becoming the dominant QC architecture.

bear.rationale: Bear: Competition from IBM/Google free-tier cloud QC suppresses IONQ pricing power. Gross margins continue declining (40%→near zero) as hardware costs don't scale. Revenue crawls to ~$260M by year 5 but persistent losses require multiple dilutive raises. Company survives as a research-grade platform but never achieves commercial scale. No quantum advantage demonstrated for enterprise workloads. shareChange +4%/yr reflects ongoing dilution for cash burn.

base.rationale: Base: IonQ captures meaningful quantum cloud market share via AWS/Azure/GCP partnerships. Revenue scales to ~$990M by year 5 as enterprises pay premium for higher-accuracy trapped-ion compute on optimization and simulation workloads. Gross margins stabilize and operating leverage kicks in — barely profitable at year 5 (5% net margin). exitPE 40x reflects early-stage profitability on a high-growth platform. Catalyst: 2-3 large enterprise SLAs plus government contracts.

bull.rationale: Bull: IonQ demonstrates quantum advantage on logistics/pharma/finance optimization. Becomes the dominant trapped-ion infrastructure layer analogous to NVIDIA in GPU compute. Revenue scales to ~$2.1B by year 5. 12% net margin from cloud-native operating leverage. QM 1.10: trapped-ion accuracy moat (higher fidelity than superconducting at equivalent qubit counts) — one identifiable structural advantage. exitPE 60x reflects dominant position in an emerging platform market. Catalyst: Named quantum advantage proof + Fortune 500 multi-year contracts.

aiThesis.rationale: IonQ at $48.02 trades at ~135x TTM revenue of $130M. Revenue grew 428% YoY demonstrating genuine commercial traction via AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, and Google Cloud. However, gross margins are declining (73%→40%) and net losses deepened to -$510M TTM. The DCF model (FV $8.54) explicitly cannot capture 10-20 year platform optionality — the market is pricing a $100B+ outcome, not a $8 one. For a 5-year horizon, the stock is deeply overvalued. As a long-duration speculative position in the thesis, IONQ is the strongest quantum computing bet available: most real revenue, most commercial relationships, differentiated trapped-ion technology with higher accuracy vs IBM/Google superconducting at equivalent qubit counts. The investment case requires accepting that DCF is the wrong tool and replacing it with a probability-weighted technology adoption curve view.
